16:1.sourceText: Καὶ διαγενομένου τοῦ σαββάτου Μαρία ἡ Μαγδαληνὴ καὶ Μαρία ἡ τοῦ Ἰακώβου καὶ Σαλώμη ἠγόρασαν ἀρώματα ἵνα ἐλθοῦσαι ἀλείψωσιν αὐτόν.
16:1.targetText: And the Sabbath having past, Mary the Magdalene, and Mary of James, and Salome, bought spices, that having come, they may anoint Him,

groups.note: The actual elapsed/passed participle διαγενομένου is rendered by the installed LSV wording having past; the printed English form is preserved rather than silently corrected to passed.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

16:2.sourceText: καὶ λίαν πρωῒ τῇ μιᾷ τῶν σαββάτων ἔρχονται ἐπὶ τὸ μνῆμα, ἀνατείλαντος τοῦ ἡλίου.
16:2.targetText: and early in the morning of the first [day] of the weeks, they come to the tomb, at the rising of the sun,

groups.note: The feminine numeral one in this calendrical expression designates the first day; LSV supplies day in brackets to state its implicit temporal head, without a separately written Greek day noun.
The genitive-absolute sun-rising participle marks the time of arrival; LSV renders the event nominally at the rising, rather than inventing a source rising noun.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek λίαν intensifies the early morning as very early; LSV does not separately express very at that occurrence.

16:3.sourceText: καὶ ἔλεγον πρὸς ἑαυτάς Τίς ἀποκυλίσει ἡμῖν τὸν λίθον ἐκ τῆς θύρας τοῦ μνημείου;
16:3.targetText: and they said among themselves, “Who will roll away the stone out of the door of the tomb for us?”

16:4.sourceText: καὶ ἀναβλέψασαι θεωροῦσιν ὅτι ἀνακεκύλισται ὁ λίθος· ἦν γὰρ μέγας σφόδρα.
16:4.targetText: And having looked, they see that the stone has been rolled away—for it was very great,

16:5.sourceText: καὶ εἰσελθοῦσαι εἰς τὸ μνημεῖον εἶδον νεανίσκον καθήμενον ἐν τοῖς δεξιοῖς περιβεβλημένον στολὴν λευκήν, καὶ ἐξεθαμβήθησαν.
16:5.targetText: and having entered into the tomb, they saw a young man sitting on the right hand, clothed in a long white robe, and they were amazed.

groups.note: The robe noun στολή denotes the long/full garment; English expands that actual garment description as a long robe, with in expressing the clothing complement rather than a separately printed Greek preposition.

16:6.sourceText: ὁ δὲ λέγει αὐταῖς Μὴ ἐκθαμβεῖσθε· Ἰησοῦν ζητεῖτε τὸν Ναζαρηνὸν τὸν ἐσταυρωμένον· ἠγέρθη, οὐκ ἔστιν ὧδε· ἴδε ὁ τόπος ὅπου ἔθηκαν αὐτόν.
16:6.targetText: And he says to them, “Do not be amazed, you seek Jesus the Nazarene, the crucified [One]: He rose—He is not here; behold the place where they laid Him!

groups.note: The actual ἠγέρθη is passive He was raised; LSV He rose uses an intransitive English resurrection predicate, with the same event retained without inventing an active source verb.

16:7.sourceText: ἀλλὰ ὑπάγετε εἴπατε τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ καὶ τῷ Πέτρῳ ὅτι Προάγει ὑμᾶς εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν· ἐκεῖ αὐτὸν ὄψεσθε, καθὼς εἶπεν ὑμῖν.
16:7.targetText: And go, say to His disciples and Peter that He goes before you to Galilee; there you will see Him, as He said to you.”

groups.note: Greek ἀλλά introduces the contrasting instruction but go; LSV connects the directive as And go, retaining the discourse turn without claiming that ἀλλά always means and.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

16:8.sourceText: καὶ ἐξελθοῦσαι ἔφυγον ἀπὸ τοῦ μνημείου, εἶχεν γὰρ αὐτὰς τρόμος καὶ ἔκστασις· καὶ οὐδενὶ οὐδὲν εἶπαν· ἐφοβοῦντο γάρ.
16:8.targetText: And having come forth quickly, they fled from the tomb, and trembling and amazement had seized them, and they said to no one anything, for they were afraid. [[

groups.note: Greek no-thing under no-one is negative concord; English anything retains that already negative scope.

unmappedSource.reason: Witness connective difference: pinned N1904 γάρ explains for trembling had seized them; LSV and follows TR δέ at this clause.

unmappedTarget.reason: The quickly adverb follows additional TR ταχύ, absent from pinned N1904.
Witness connective difference: LSV and follows TR δέ while N1904 has explanatory γάρ before the trembling clause.

review.note: LSV opens double brackets for the following longer ending at the end of this verse; pinned N1904 preserves that longer ending too, opening its own double brackets at 16:9 and closing at 16:20. The actual supplied Greek 16:9–20 words are mapped in their own references, not treated as an absent witness or invented source text.

16:9.sourceText: [[Ἀναστὰς δὲ πρωῒ πρώτῃ σαββάτου ἐφάνη πρῶτον Μαρίᾳ τῇ Μαγδαληνῇ, παρ’ ἧς ἐκβεβλήκει ἑπτὰ δαιμόνια.
16:9.targetText: And He, having risen in the morning of the first of the week, appeared first to Mary the Magdalene, out of whom He had cast seven demons;

review.note: The pinned N1904 source itself includes this longer ending in double brackets. Its exact raw opening token [[Ἀναστὰς is retained, and the actual word—not an invented unbracketed replacement—is the resurrection source anchor.

16:10.sourceText: ἐκείνη πορευθεῖσα ἀπήγγειλεν τοῖς μετ’ αὐτοῦ γενομένοις πενθοῦσι καὶ κλαίουσιν·
16:10.targetText: she having gone, told those who had been with Him, mourning and weeping;

16:11.sourceText: κἀκεῖνοι ἀκούσαντες ὅτι ζῇ καὶ ἐθεάθη ὑπ’ αὐτῆς ἠπίστησαν.
16:11.targetText: and they, having heard that He is alive, and was seen by her, did not believe.

groups.note: The actual privative believing verb ἠπίστησαν means disbelieved; English did not believe expresses that one head without a separately written Greek negative particle.

16:12.sourceText: Μετὰ δὲ ταῦτα δυσὶν ἐξ αὐτῶν περιπατοῦσιν ἐφανερώθη ἐν ἑτέρᾳ μορφῇ πορευομένοις εἰς ἀγρόν·
16:12.targetText: And after these things, to two of them, as they are going into a field, walking, He appeared in another form,

groups.note: The circumstantial going participle describes those same two recipients in motion; LSV expands it as as they are going without an independently printed as or they word.

16:13.sourceText: κἀκεῖνοι ἀπελθόντες ἀπήγγειλαν τοῖς λοιποῖς· οὐδὲ ἐκείνοις ἐπίστευσαν.
16:13.targetText: and they having gone, told [it] to the rest; not even them did they believe.

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English it supplies the reported content; N1904 has no independent object pronoun or stated content noun at told here.

16:14.sourceText: Ὕστερον δὲ ἀνακειμένοις αὐτοῖς τοῖς ἕνδεκα ἐφανερώθη, καὶ ὠνείδισεν τὴν ἀπιστίαν αὐτῶν καὶ σκληροκαρδίαν ὅτι τοῖς θεασαμένοις αὐτὸν ἐγηγερμένον οὐκ ἐπίστευσαν.
16:14.targetText: Afterward, as they are reclining, He appeared to the Eleven, and reproached their unbelief and stiffness of heart, because they did not believe those having seen Him being raised;

groups.note: The circumstantial reclining participle is recast as a temporal as ... are reclining clause.
The actual dative pronoun identifies the Eleven as reclining persons and appearance recipients; English uses nominative they in the temporal reclining clause for those same people.

The actual perfect passive ἐγηγερμένον describes Him in the completed raised state. LSV being raised preserves the resurrection head but does not establish that the witnesses watched an ongoing raising process.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek connective δέ has no separate English counterpart after Afterward.
Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

16:15.sourceText: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Πορευθέντες εἰς τὸν κόσμον ἅπαντα κηρύξατε τὸ εὐαγγέλιον πάσῃ τῇ κτίσει.
16:15.targetText: and He said to them, “Having gone into all the world, proclaim the good news to all the creation;

16:16.sourceText: ὁ πιστεύσας καὶ βαπτισθεὶς σωθήσεται, ὁ δὲ ἀπιστήσας κατακριθήσεται.
16:16.targetText: he who has believed and has been immersed will be saved; and he who has not believed will be condemned.

groups.note: The actual ἀπιστήσας is the privative disbelieving participle, rendered has not believed; not belongs to that genuine verb rather than a new negative token.

16:17.sourceText: σημεῖα δὲ τοῖς πιστεύσασιν ταῦτα παρακολουθήσει, ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί μου δαιμόνια ἐκβαλοῦσιν, γλώσσαις λαλήσουσιν καιναῖς,
16:17.targetText: And signs will accompany those believing these things: they will cast out demons in My Name; they will speak with new tongues;

groups.note: The neuter plural ταῦτα commonly points to these signs in the Greek clause; LSV attaches these things to believing as its content. The actual demonstrative is retained with this source/target scope difference explicit, without adding a Greek things or message noun.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

16:18.sourceText: ὄφεις ἀροῦσιν κἂν θανάσιμόν τι πίωσιν οὐ μὴ αὐτοὺς βλάψῃ, ἐπὶ ἀρρώστους χεῖρας ἐπιθήσουσιν καὶ καλῶς ἕξουσιν.
16:18.targetText: they will take up serpents; and if they may drink any deadly thing, it will not hurt them; they will lay hands on the ailing, and they will be well.”

groups.note: The καλῶς ἕξουσιν idiom literally has well/will-have and expresses being in a good condition; LSV they will be well renders that complete health-state construction, not a separately printed Greek be verb.

16:19.sourceText: Ὁ μὲν οὖν Κύριος Ἰησοῦς μετὰ τὸ λαλῆσαι αὐτοῖς ἀνελήμφθη εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ ἐκάθισεν ἐκ δεξιῶν τοῦ Θεοῦ.
16:19.targetText: The LORD, then, indeed, after speaking to them, was received up to Heaven, and sat on the right hand of God;

unmappedSource.reason: Pinned N1904 explicitly adds the Jesus name with the Lord, Ἰησοῦς; LSV/TR has only the LORD at this occurrence. The name is not silently moved to another word.
Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

16:20.sourceText: ἐκεῖνοι δὲ ἐξελθόντες ἐκήρυξαν πανταχοῦ, τοῦ Κυρίου συνεργοῦντος καὶ τὸν λόγον βεβαιοῦντος διὰ τῶν ἐπακολουθούντων σημείων.]]
16:20.targetText: and they, having gone forth, preached everywhere, the LORD working with [them], and confirming the word, through the signs following. Amen.]]

groups.note: The actual preachers ἐκεῖνοι are the same people with whom the Lord immediately cooperates in the accompanying genitive-absolute clause. English repeats those real semantic partners as bracketed them; no additional Greek object pronoun is invented, and the single stated people identity is retained across its subject/partner roles.

unmappedTarget.reason: The closing Amen is printed by LSV but absent from the pinned N1904 longer-ending text, which closes after the signs phrase.

review.note: The exact Greek longer-ending closing token σημείων.]] is preserved. Double-bracket punctuation is part of the displayed source witness; the English Amen addition is separately explained and does not create an original Greek Amen word.

16:99.sourceText: [[Πάντα δὲ τὰ παρηγγελμένα τοῖς περὶ τὸν Πέτρον συντόμως ἐξήγγειλαν. Μετὰ δὲ ταῦτα καὶ αὐτὸς ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἀπὸ ἀνατολῆς καὶ ἄχρι δύσεως ἐξαπέστειλεν δι’ αὐτῶν τὸ ἱερὸν καὶ ἄφθαρτον κήρυγμα τῆς αἰωνίου σωτηρίας.]]

The actual raw Greek words are explained here without inventing English counterparts or moving them into the different longer ending.
